configs.description: Two 1500 W AC supplies, back-to-front airflow. No document draws this build, so it is drawn like the F2B one; see the b2f-finish gap.

gaps.wanted: Where the OSFP ports' own lamps are. The guide's Port Descriptions table gives every OSFP port a lamp (green 100G per lane, amber 50G or lower, on or blinking) and the Front Panel callout points "Indicator LED - OSFP" at the port block, but neither the figure nor the render shows a window for one: the band between the rows carries only the printed legend and the cages' latch notches, and the triangles are ink. No lamp is placed rather than one guessed at. A photograph of a powered unit settles it.

What the round grey dot at (104.3, 7.6) on the Front Panel figure is. It sits beside the upper SFP+ lamp, the size of the lamp but grey; the three-quarter render draws a vent cell there. It could be an unlit lamp, a reset pinhole or a drawing artefact. Two small dark squares above the SYS lamp (about 319.8 and 322.2, y 7.2) are equally unexplained. Neither is drawn.

The DC build's supply. The What's in the Box table lists R4035-F9007-A1, "DC PSU 2x1500W, F2B", and the Ground Lug Installation page exists for it ("not applicable to the AC SKU versions"), but no figure draws a DC supply's face, so the DC build is not offered as a configuration.

Which end FAN1 and PSU1 are. The Rear Panel LEDs table names FAN1-FAN7 and PSU1/PSU2 and no figure labels a bay. The bays are numbered left to right as seen from the rear because a view has to order them somehow; no numeral is printed.
What colour the back-to-front build's fan handles and latches are. Only the F2B build is drawn anywhere; many vendors mark B2F modules in a second colour, and whether this one does is not shown.

Orthographic drawings of the lid, underside and side walls. The three-quarter renders show a plain grey lid with a recessed label or handle plate towards the rear and slide-rail screw heads along the sides, which cannot be measured from a perspective render.

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor
one of `power-max-w`, `power-max-ac-w`, `power-max-dc-w` in `attrs.power` (profile `networking` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices
`physical-context` on 9 bays (rear 9); `physical-context` on port group osfp - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

airflow.note: The What's in the Box table lists R4035-F9001-A1 (F2B), R4035-F9005-A1 (B2F) and R4035-F9007-A1 (DC PSU 2x1500W, F2B). Every figure shows the F2B build's orange fans; no document shows what the B2F build's trays or latches look like, so the B2F configuration is drawn identically and says so.

colour.note: Front plate #2a2a2a sampled between features on the Front Panel Callouts figure; the three-quarter render agrees (black). Rear sheet metal #a7a9ac sampled on the rear figure's left strip.

fans-and-supplies-are-shared-with-the-ds.note: THE SAME SHAPES, MEASURED ON THIS DEVICE'S OWN FIGURE. celestica/psu-1500-ac@1 and celestica/fan-40@1 were drawn off the DS4000 guide. Checked against the DS4100 rear here: PSU lamps at module (6.65, 25.55) and (6.65, 31.75) against the part's (6.5, 25.4) and (6.5, 32.1); the fan lamp at module (3.05, 3.55) against (3.7, 3.6); fan pitch 44.02 against 43.96. Faces here measure 0.5 wider than the parts on both (55.7 against 55.2, and the orange tray about 40 against 39.3), which is the frame gap being read as module at 3.9 px/mm and is recorded, not reconciled. THE FAN IS ORANGE HERE AND BLACK ON THE DS4000. Face and handle are sampled at #dd8817 on the figure and on the render; they are fan-40's face-finish and handle-finish fields, set by the configuration, not a second part. Sampled on the rear figure at the handle band's left end (fan 2): the latch reads #be7515, a shade darker than the band's #d68415 - no blue anywhere, so latch-finish and handle-finish take those two values and face-finish #dd8817. The supplies' latch at the far right is drawn black on this figure where the DS4000 part defaults to orange, so latch-finish is set #1f2124 too.

gate-1.note: BOTH CALLOUT FIGURES ARE ORTHOGRAPHIC. The Front Panel Callouts figure's dark face box reads 1789 x 176 px (x 20-1808, y 196-371) against the stated 438.5 x 43.1 mm: aspect 10.165 against 10.174, 0.09% out, 4.080 px/mm across and 4.083 down. The Rear Panel Callouts figure reads 1710 x 169 px (x 15-1724, y 111-279), aspect 10.118, 0.55% out, 3.900 and 3.921 px/mm. Both are about 1.7x the resolution of the System Overview elevations of the same faces (2.34 and 2.50 px/mm), so every position on this device is read off the two callout figures. The side thumbscrew knobs drawn beyond both ends of the front are outside the body box and are not modelled; no ear is drawn.

legends.note: Read on the Front Panel Callouts figure and confirmed as printed on the three-quarter render: `N (up)(down) N+1` centred on each column in the band between the rows, digits about 1.6 mm tall (cap) - column 1's spans x 129.2-136.2 centred 21.9; `M1 (up)(down) M2` between the SFP+ cages; SYS, FAN, PSU and ALM to the left of the four system lamps; CONSOLE, the USB SuperSpeed mark and MGMT printed vertically to the right of the management housing, reading bottom to top; LUG TAG above the pull-out tag; and the Celestica wordmark as plain text at upper left (x 17.5-40.5). The SS mark is drawn as the letters SS only - the trident beside it is not drawn. The triangles are drawn as ink, not lamps: they are the same white as the numerals on both the figure and the render, and the SFP+ legend carries the same triangles while its lamps are separate green domes.

lifecycle.note: Listed as a current platform on cls.celestica.com/hardware-platforms/ds4100/ when fetched on 2026-09-26; no end-of-life notice was found there or on the documentation portal, whose guide was last revised 3/2026.

lug-tag.note: celestica/lug-tag-ridge-23@1 - the top-ridge card, the same 23.3 mm part as the ES1000's - seated flat (rotate 0). The Front Panel figure reads its slot x 383.0-405.8 from y 38.3 to the bottom edge, centre x 394.4, so at = (394.4 - 11.65, 38.5). The vendor render ds4100-A.png draws the card with a hatched grip along its TOP edge over its middle, rounded ends and no end block, and the guide figure a raised centre - the ridge form, not celestica/lug-tag@1's end-lip card. The render prints DS4100 on the card and LUG TAG on the panel above it.

power.note: The datasheet's Power and Cooling: "1+1 redundant, hot swap PSUs, 1500W", "AC 47~63Hz, 100~240 V nominal, 90~264V max", "6+1 redundant fans, front to back and back to front airflow", "Power consumption, Max 1310W". The guide's table repeats 1310 W max. 1310 W is the chassis maximum and is recorded as the vendor's figure; it is not reconciled against module draws.

rear.note: Rear Panel Callouts figure at 3.90 px/mm. Two supplies in the SAME orientation (not mirrored): frames x 10.5-66.4 and 377.2-432.9, about 55.7 wide and 40.5 tall; each carries a lattice grille at left with two lamps at its foot - "!" over a check mark, the callout's "Top - alarm, Bottom - OK" - a black U-grip, a C14 inlet turned a quarter and a latch at the far right. Bays are drawn at celestica/psu-1500-ac@1's own 55.2 x 39.0 (read by the DS4000 modeller on that guide) centred on the frames measured here. Seven orange fan modules: the orange faces at y 3 run 70.52-108.73, 114.63-152.83 ... 334.64- 372.85, a 44.02 mm pitch; across the handle bar they read 40.26 wide and top to bottom 2.30 to 40.80. Bays use celestica/fan-40@1's 39.3 x 39.0 centred on those. At the far left two round screw heads (x 5.7, y 24.1 and 33.4, about 5 mm across) - the two M3 holes the Ground Lug Installation page fixes the ground-lug bracket to at this corner.

sources.note: Two documents and two vendor renders. The DS4100 installation guide (Celestica documentation portal, HTML, release 1.3.1 3/2026) carries the System Specifications table, a front elevation and a rear elevation (system-overview-1/-3, 2.3-2.5 px/mm), a Front Panel Callouts figure with the LED and port tables, a Rear Panel Callouts figure with its LED table, the What's in the Box SKU table and the Ground Lug Installation photographs. The DS4100 datasheet carries the features, power, dimensions and approvals. cls.celestica.com/hardware-platforms/ds4100/ serves two three-quarter renders (front, and front+rear side by side), saved as working/intake/celestica/photos/ds4100-A.png and -AB.png; they are perspective and are used only for colour, counts and legends, never for position.

the-management-housing.note: ONE SILVER HOUSING, x 328.4-345.2 by y 7.4-40.0, stacking console (top, latch slot up), USB Type-A (middle) and MGMT (bottom, its latch slot and lamps at the bottom) - the guide's callout: "Top - 1 x Console, Middle - 1 x USB Type A 3.0, Bottom - 1 x Ethernet RJ45". The housing is panel decor (the metal shell the jacks sit in); the jacks are std/rj45-ganged@2 cells (12.7 x 11.0, which is what a stacked shell's cells measure - about 11 mm per jack here) and std/usb-a@1, centred on the housing at x 336.8. the console cell is turned 180 so its latch slot is at the top, as drawn, and MGMT is common/rj45-ganged-eth@1 upright, whose lamps sit in the latch-side (bottom) corners, where the figure draws two small light squares; the LED table names them (right: green 1000M / amber 10-100M; left: green link / blinking activity).

the-osfp-wall.note: TWO BLOCKS OF FOUR STACKED COLUMNS. The bright cage walls inside the openings, profiled across the face at y 8, 12, 16, 28 and 34 mm, put the inner dividers of block 1 at 144.49, 167.66 and 190.94 and of block 2 at 245.85, 269.13 and 292.36 - an in-block pitch of 23.24 (23.225 and 23.255 per block) and a block pitch of 101.48, which leaves an 8.5 mm gutter between blocks. Column 1 is centred at 132.87. The aperture rows read 6.12-19.10 and 24.98-37.96 on a vertical profile through column 1, so 12.98 mm tall against std/osfp@1's 23.1 x 13.5 registry-drawn aperture, which is seated centred on each (the part owns the aperture, the device owns the pitch, as on edgecore/ais800-32o). Row pitch 18.86. At 4.08 px/mm every figure here is good to about a quarter of a millimetre. NUMBERING: the panel prints `1 (up) (down) 2` between each column's two cages and on to `15 (up) (down) 16`, so odd ports are the upper row and even the lower, numbering left to right. Upper cages are rotate 0 and lower 180, AND THAT IS A READING, NOT A RULE (#799): an OSFP stack is held to the same way up (L108), and this one is built otherwise. The callout figure draws each lower cage as the upper turned over - the upper's card slot low in its opening with two retention bumps on its top edge, the lower's card slot high with its bumps on its bottom edge - and the 18.86 row pitch is neither of the OSFP MSA's stacked-cage pitches (14.9, 19.9) but leaves room for the host board between the rows: two single cages either side of one board (OSFP MSA rev 5.22 section 7.6). The render ds4100-A.png agrees as far as it shows: the lower cage's top edge carries dark notches where the upper's carries raised bumps. Each pair is named in stack-exceptions.

the-sfp-pair-and-its-lamps.note: A stacked 1x2 SFP cage at x 93.63-108.58, frames y 10.29-20.82 and 23.26-33.55; std/sfp@1 (14.5 x 10) is centred on each, upper 0 and lower 180. One green lamp above (98.17, 7.72) and one below (98.17, 36.61), each 2.2 mm across - common/led-dot@1. The guide's callout names them "Indicator LED - SFP28" and the LED table's SFP+ rows give Green 10GbE / Amber 1GbE, on and blinking. The upper lamp is taken as M1's and the lower as M2's by position; no document says so. THE FIGURE ALSO DRAWS A GREY DOT at (104.3, 7.6), right of the upper lamp, 1.8 mm across. The render shows a vent cell there, not a dot. It is not drawn; see the grey-dot gap.

the-system-lamps.note: Four green domes 3.4 mm across at x 324.15, y 12.25, 17.39, 22.53 and 27.68 - a 5.14 mm pitch. common/led-indicator@1 (4 x 4, 2 mm lamp) is seated on the centres. States from the guide's LED Descriptions table: SYS green/amber alternate blinking = normal, off = no power; FAN and PSU green = all normal, amber = one absent or abnormal; ALM green = no alarm, amber = critical, amber 4 Hz = major, amber 1 Hz = minor. The alternate green/amber blink is recorded as green blinking; the table gives no rate for it.

vent-fields.note: Extents read on the Front Panel Callouts figure: a left column x 1.0-13.4, a two-row strip x 15.0-75.5 by y 3.0-7.8, a field x 20.8-59.4 by y 15.0-35.6 under the wordmark, a two-row patch x 79.0-92.0 by y 26.5-31.6 beside the SFP+ cages, and on the right a band x 350-425 by y 1.5-10.5, a field x 378-416.5 by y 15-35.5 and a column x 424-433. The cells are drawn with the grille pattern (dark square cells; the slots pattern paints its cells lighter than this plate) at the measured pitches (about 2.45 x 3.0); the true cells are narrower rectangles than the pattern draws, so the texture is indicative and the extents are the measurement.
